title: Panel choreography and micro-bootcamp onboarding
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical playbook blending two adjacent needs: (1) a repeatable choreography for interview panels that reduces scheduling friction and normalizes scoring across roles, and (2) a ‘micro-bootcamp’ onboarding checklist for the first 30 days focused on ramp velocity and early impact.

Why this exists (problem statement):
- Panels are inconsistent: different teams run wildly different flows, which makes score normalization hard and lengthens time-to-offer.
- New hires (esp. ICs and interns) need a small, prescriptive first-30 plan that integrates product context, systems access, and a mentor cadence.
- We want to reduce candidate dropout and reduce first-30-day confusion for new hires.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: hiring managers, interviewers, recruiters, and people-ops onboarding leads.
- Roles covered: backend infra, serving runtime engineers, SRE, product engineers, product managers (basic variant), and intern/early-career ICs.

High-level outcomes we care about:
- Consistent interview experience (same approx length, same rubric dimensions)
- Average time-to-offer for SWE roles reduced by 15% (target)
- New-hire first-week checklist completion >= 90%
- First-30 deliverable completed for 80% of hires

Part A — Panel choreography (one-page cheat sheet):
1) Core principles:
   - 60–75 minute total panel with 3 interviewers + debrief (virtual)
   - Each interviewer owns one rubric dimension (see scorecard mapping below)
   - Candidate receives the schedule, interviewer names, and role focus 24 hours before
   - Start with 5min intro + context (hiring manager) to set expectations
   - End with 5min candidate Q&A + next steps (recruiter)

2) Timeline (60m standard):
   - 00:00–05:00 Intro & setup (HM: role context, stretch goals, team vibe)
   - 05:00–25:00 Technical deep-dive (engineer interviewer)
   - 25:00–40:00 System design / architecture (senior engineer or tech lead)
   - 40:00–55:00 Behavioral & product judgment (manager or PM)
   - 55:00–60:00 Candidate Qs & wrap (recruiter outlines next steps)

3) Logistics notes:
   - Use shared calendar block with Zoom + recording enabled (consent check)
   - Recruiter posts panel brief in #hiring-shadow on Slack 30 min before
   - Interviewers must complete preliminary rubric within 24h after the call; scoring later than 48h flags the packet for recruiter follow-up

4) Common interview traps and mitigation:
   - Trap: interviewers drift into unrelated code-review minutiae — mitigation: use the question prompt and timebox to the stated goal.
   - Trap: inconsistent difficulty across candidates — mitigation: use one of the canonical question sets (see appendix) and adapt only for role-scope, not complexity.

Part B — Scorecard (single standardized rubric) 
- Dimensions (each scored 1–5 with short evidence/comments):
   1) Core technical competence (algorithms/data structures or infra-specific skills)
   2) System design & tradeoffs (capacity planning, latency, cost)
   3) Product judgment & impact orientation (clarity on product metrics, prioritization)
   4) Communication & collaboration (clarity, listening, async culture fit)
   5) Ownership & execution (examples of drive, shipping under constraints)
- Passing threshold: average >= 3.5 across dimensions and no dimension scored a 1.
- Tiebreaker: prioritize evidence of ownership + product judgment for mission-aligned hires.

Part C — Canonical question sets (short samples)
- Infra-engineer technical deep-dive (20m):
   * Memory/kv-cache question: describe a KV cache for embeddings at 1M keys — how to handle TTL, compaction, and hot keys? (expected signals: eviction policy, sharding, cold-start mitigation)
   * Complexity followup: what is the tail-latency implication for synchronous vs async cache warming?
- System design (15m):
   * Design an inference routing layer that can choose among models by latency/cost policy. Sketch components, failure modes, and a fallback strategy. (expected: routing policy, circuit breakers, metrics to surface).
- Behavioral (15m):
   * Tell us about a time you shipped a design that degraded performance temporarily to reduce cost. What was your decision-making framework? (expected: tradeoffs, stakeholder communication, rollback plan).

Part D — Interviewer preparation checklist (short):
- Read candidate resume top-to-bottom (3 min)
- Review role brief + hiring rubric (1 pager)
- Pick 1 clarifying question you will ask the candidate at the start
- After interview: enter 2–3 lines of evidence + numeric score into the hiring form within 24h

Part E — Micro-bootcamp onboarding (first 30 days):
Objective: enable a new hire to make a narrowly scoped, measurable contribution within 30 days and be productive in team processes.

0) Pre-start (day -3 to 0):
- Hardware: laptop imaged and shipped (or ready at office)
- Access: email, Slack, SSO, GitHub org, CI dashboard, cloud console (read-only) provisioned
- Welcome packet: team org chart, 30-day goals, mentor assignment, first-week schedule
- Note: if any access blocked >day 1, escalate to ops-channel and mark in the onboarding tracker

1) Day 1 checklist (in-person or remote):
- 09:00–10:00: Welcome + HR intro (benefits, payroll)
- 10:00–11:00: Team intro + 1:1 with hiring manager (role expectations) continued
- 11:00–12:00: Engineering setup session with buddy (repo checkouts, dev container, test run)
- Lunch: team intro lunch (virtual meet-and-greet)
- 14:00–16:00: Small first task assigned (README fix + unit test) to validate local setup
- End-of-day: 15-min sync with buddy to surface any blockers

2) Week 1 objectives:
- Complete environment + CI run (green on CI for a basic change)
- Read the product brief + 1 technical postmortem from the team
- Deliver the first small task with a PR and receive at least one review

3) Week 2–4 (30-day micro-sprint):
- Week 2: Shadow on-call rotations / observability runbook read-through; pick a tiny bug to fix in a production-adjacent repo
- Week 3: Own a small feature or infra change that has a narrow scope and measurable outcome (e.g., reduce a cold-start p95 by X ms in a local dev harness or add a dashboard metric)
- Week 4: Demo the change to the team; 30-day review with manager and mentor to surface learnings and next steps

4) Mentor/buddy cadence:
- Buddy: schedule daily 15-min standups week1, then 3x/week week2–4
- Manager: weekly 30-min check-ins (focus on blockers + career context)
- Hiring manager: 30-day review (structured: what went well, what to improve, clear 60-day deliverable)

5) Success criteria for 30-day micro-bootcamp:
- Technical setup: dev environment and CI green with PRs merged
- Deliverable: at least one measurable change merged and deployed to staging
- Social: met with >=6 cross-functional partners (SRE, product, design, infra)
- Feedback: mentor and manager rate new hire >= 3 on ramp progress scale (1–5)

Part F — Lightweight hiring plan template (quarterly sprint):
- Headcount ask: x FTE by quarter end (role-level breakdown)
- Priority tiers: 1 (mission critical), 2 (near-term), 3 (nice-to-have)
- Candidate pipeline targets: 3 active screens per open role, 1 onsite/offered per role per 4 weeks
- Recruiter SLA: initial candidate outreach within 4 business days of req approval

Part G — Open questions & TODOs (notes to self):
- We should A/B the 60m panel vs a 45m + homework take-home for senior infra roles (explore metrics: candidate acceptance rate, time-to-offer).
- Need canonical question bank per level for infra and SRE (owner: Priya).
- Create a short interviewer training video (5–7m) showing debrief norms and evidence-based scoring.
- Integrate the 30-day micro-bootcamp into the onboarding tracker (JIRA-HIRE-842) so EMs can assign tasks from templates.

Appendix & references:
- Quick link: onboarding tracker (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PEOPLE/Onboarding+Tracker)
- Example PR rubric and DEI guidance: see linked Confluence playbook

Footer notes (tone & cultural bits):
- Keep interviews curious and human-centered — we want to evaluate for learning ability and humility, not just memorized answers.
- This doc intentionally errs on the side of compactness — use it as a lightweight scaffold, not a rigid script.

-- Adriana (notes: present this at People Ops sync 2026-01-14)
